subject: Maths
title: Factorising expressions
subtitle: Algebraic Expressions · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can factorise algebraic expressions by taking out common factors.

key_vocab.definition: Factorising is the reverse of expanding. We find a common factor and write the expression as a product of terms.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can factorise algebraic expressions by taking out common factors.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Factorising -- Factorising is the reverse of expanding. We find a common factor and write the expression as a product of terms.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Find the highest common factor (HCF) of all terms. Write it outside the bracket. Divide each term by the HCF to get what goes inside.
4x² + 8x = 4x(x + 2)
HCF = 4x; divide each term by 4x

Key examples:
  ✓ 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3)  (HCF is 3)
  ✓ x² + 5x = x(x + 5)  (HCF is x)
  ✓ 4x² + 8x = 4x(x + 2)  (HCF is 4x)
  ✗ 6x + 9 = 6(x + 3)  (6 is not a factor of 9)
  ✗ x² + 5x = x(x + 5x)  (divided only first term)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – number HCF
  Factorise 6x + 9
  HCF of 6 and 9 is 3
  6x ÷ 3 = 2x; 9 ÷ 3 = 3
  Write: 3(2x + 3)
  = 3(2x + 3)
  (Check by expanding: 3 × 2x + 3 × 3 = 6x + 9 ✓)

Example 2 – letter HCF
  Factorise x² + 5x
  Both terms contain x
  x² ÷ x = x; 5x ÷ x = 5
  Write: x(x + 5)
  = x(x + 5)
  (Take out the lowest power of x from each term.)

sections.title: Letter common factor
sections.content:
Take out the highest power of the letter.

(a) x² + 3x
(b) x² − 7x
(c) 2x² + x
(d) 5x² − 10x

sections.title: Number and letter HCF
sections.content:
Find the full HCF (number and letter).

(a) 6x² + 12x
(b) 8x² − 4x
(c) 9x² + 3x
(d) 10x³ + 15x²

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3)
✗ x² + 5x = x(x + 5x)
✓ 4x² + 8x = 4x(x + 2)
✗ 6x + 9 = 6(x + 1.5)
✓ Factorising is the reverse of expanding

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Number common factor:
  (a) 4(x + 2)
  (b) 3(2x + 5)
  (c) 5(2x − 1)
  (d) 6(2x + 3)

Letter common factor:
  (a) x(x + 3)
  (b) x(x − 7)
  (c) x(2x + 1)
  (d) 5x(x − 2)

Number and letter HCF:
  (a) 6x(x + 2)
  (b) 4x(2x − 1)
  (c) 3x(3x + 1)
  (d) 5x²(2x + 3)

Three-term expressions:
  (a) 3(x² + 2x + 3)
  (b) 5(x² − 2x + 3)
  (c) 4(x² + 2x + 3)
  (d) 2x(x² + 2x + 3)

Mixed factorising:
  (a) 7(x + 3)
  (b) x(x + 4)
  (c) 4x(3x − 2)
  (d) 5(3x² + 2x + 1)
  (e) 3x²(2x − 3)
